extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners; patent applicants and practitioners (KIPO procedures)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how examiners should accept/refuse applicant amendments, suggest amendments (positive examination), perform ex‑officio amendments, and initiate ex‑officio re‑examination under the Korean Patent Act. Covers procedural and substantive criteria, examples, and prohibited practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal to enter amendment within 30 days from the filing of an appeal shall fall under: (①) Where the amendment does not comply with requirements for amendment under Article 47(2)-(3) of the Patent Act; ② Where new grounds for rejection are deemed to be arisen from the amendment (‘deletion of claim(s)’ excluded among amendments according to Article 47(3), subparagraph 1-4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grounds for rejection previously notified are not overcome by the amendment within 30 days from filing of an appeal, but no new reasons arise from the amendment, the amendment shall be accepted but the original decision stands. If prior grounds are not overcome AND new grounds arise from the amendment, the amendment shall be refused to be entered and review proceeds based on the specification before the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation for introduction of new matter (Article 47(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing whether an amendment introduces new matter under Article 47(2), the amendment shall be compared with the specification or drawings of the originally filed patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This comparison is used when the amendment is alleged to introduce subject-matter not originally filed (new matter). Applicable even where amendments are submitted after various stages of examination/reconsideration as described in examples (compare with orig. filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation for amendment requirements (Article 47(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether an amendment satisfies the requirements under Article 47(3) shall be performed by comparing the amendment with the specification or drawings of the relevant prior amendment (e.g., amendment II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, whether the scope of claims is narrowed shall be determined by comparing corresponding claims between the earlier amendment (e.g., amendment II) and the later amendment (e.g., amendment III or IV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination whether claim scope is narrowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the scope of claims is narrowed is determined by comparing corresponding claims between the prior amendment and the new amendment (e.g., amendment II vs amendment III/IV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate compliance with Article 47(3) when amendments are filed during appeal/review; governs whether the amendment is permissible as narrowing rather than broadening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for issuing notice of grounds for rejection at reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for issuing a notice of grounds for rejection during the reconsideration process: where an examiner is to make a decision to reject under Article 62, the applicant should be provided an opportunity to submit written arguments (Article 63); applications at review shall be either notified with grounds for rejection or decided as amendment refused to be entered depending on case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments within 30 days after filing appeal that violate Article 47(2) or (3) or necessitate new rejections shall be refused entry and review based on specification before amendment. If amendments do not include reasons for refusal to enter but new grounds are identified during reconsideration that were not identified before review, grounds for rejection shall be issued. Where earlier grounds existed before first notice, issue non-final rejection; where grounds arise with amendment responding to a first notice, issue final rejection necessitated by amendment; if both types arise simultaneously, issue non-final rejection. If amendment does not address grounds that led to rejection, the original decision shall stand.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to refuse entry versus notify grounds during review of post-appeal amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendments within 30 days after filing of an appeal are in violation of Article 47(2) or (3) or introduce new grounds, amendments shall be refused entry and review based on prior specification. If amendments do not include causes for refusal to enter but new grounds for rejection are identified during reconsideration, a notice of grounds shall be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application was rejected at examination with grounds not identified earlier and amendment introduces new matter, examiner shall notify grounds for rejection rather than simply refusing the amendment in some circumstances (see detailed subpoints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination after notifying grounds for rejection — outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: After reconsideration of applicant’s arguments or amendments responding to a notice of grounds for rejection, the examiner shall: (i) determine application allowable where grounds addressed; (ii) original decision shall stand where grounds not resolved; (iii) issue a notice of non-final rejection where grounds that existed before are identified again; (iv) issue a notice of final rejection necessitated by amendment if new grounds introduced by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendments violate Article 47(2) or (3) or introduce new grounds, amendments are refused entry and review is based on prior specification; if amendments do not include reasons for refusal but grounds for rejection persist, amendment accepted but original decision stands; if previously unidentified grounds are found, issue a non-final or final notice as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to grant after reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner determines that a request for appeals is reasonable in view of the results of reconsideration, the examiner shall cancel the original decision and make a decision to grant (or register the utility model), with the notice of allowance bearing the notion that 'the original decision shall be cancelled' ahead of 'the decision to grant a patent is made' (Article 54(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On grant after appeal, examiner must transmit copies of notice of allowance and relevant appeal documents to the trial policy division of IPTAB (exception: electronic file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining the original decision after reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner cannot allow a patent, he/she shall not make the decision to reject the application again, but report the results of the reconsideration to the head of the subgroup of the examination division and notify it to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When original decision stands after reconsideration (including when applicant withdraws appeal or abandons filing), examiner transmits reconsideration results and trial document file to IPTAB (electronic documents may be excepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of appeal documents after examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner makes a decision to grant after review, he/she shall transmit a copy of the notice of allowance and a file of relevant appeal documents to the trial policy division of the IPTAB; similarly, where the original decision stands and appeals are withdrawn/abandoned, a copy of results and a file of trial documents shall be transmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic files are excepted from mandatory transmittal in certain statutory provisions (Articles 53, 54).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio re-examination permissible when obvious grounds exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner finds obvious reasons for rejection after grant with respect to a patent application in question, he/she can revoke the patent ex-officio and re-examine the concerned patent application (ex-officio re-examination), except where the application falls under specified exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include: (i) grounds corresponding to Article 42(3)(ii) or (8) and Article 45; (ii) after grant the patent is registered for establishment of right; (iii) the application is withdrawn or abandoned. Ex-officio re-examination only before registration of establishment of right and when grounds are obvious and serious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio re-examination — time-wise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex-officio re-examination may be performed if establishment of right is neither registered after grant nor the patent application is withdrawn or abandoned (Article 66-3(1) of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation and re-examination can only be performed before the patent right has become established by registration/payment; if registration occurs before notification, revocation is deemed not made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio re-examination — substantive requirement (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may reexamine only where he/she finds obvious grounds for rejection (not mere possibility); the granted patent must 'obviously be invalidated' based on that ground for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere possibility of invalidation is insufficient — grounds must be obvious and serious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural safeguards for ex-officio re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before notifying revocation under ex-officio re-examination, the examiner should conduct a consultation between three concerned persons (including a director of an examination division or head of examination part and another concerned person).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should issue a first office action based on the obvious ground for rejection as early as possible (maximum 7 days) from the date of notifying revocation so applicant can file written argument. Applicant may amend a specification or drawings within the scope of the specification as filed and drawings. If grounds for rejection were notified before revocation, notify again to provide opportunity to submit written argument (Article 63(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on triggers for ex-officio re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex-officio re-examination is not permitted where the obvious ground for rejection is: (i) improper description of background art; (ii) claim(s) improperly formulated; or (iii) beyond unity of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are expressly excluded from ex-officio re-examination even if a problem is obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect when application registered or withdrawn before notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the concerned patent application has been registered or withdrawn/abandoned before the patent applicant is notified that the granted patent is revoked, the revocation shall be deemed not to have been made, and ex-officio re-examination cannot be performed (Article 66-3(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness of notification is critical: revocation procedure cannot proceed if registration/withdrawal/abandonment intervenes beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments before revocation preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of ex-officio re-examination, the amendments made before the revocation of the granted patent shall not be dismissed (Article 51(1)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier applicant amendments that were entered remain effective in the re-examination process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of newly submitted relevant information before registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant information is provided before registration with respect to a granted patent, an examiner should review whether an obvious ground for rejection exists for the granted patent based on the submitted proving document(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New evidence supplied prior to establishment of rights should prompt examiner review for possible ex-officio action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive examination — examiner may suggest amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may suggest amendments when notifying grounds for rejection so that an applicant can rapidly obtain a patent with a reasonable scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions aim to accelerate allowance with reasonable claim scope; examiner should indicate related grounds for rejection when suggesting amendments (use 'Advices on Amendment' section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Target application suitability for suggested amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner can suggest amendments for an application meeting the following requirements: ① the invention should be understandable; ② sufficient prior art search is made (except where lack of description prevents search); ③ the claimed invention has a technical feature distinguished from prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maximize effect, focus suggestions on proper scope rather than fixing lack of description. Amendments should be suggested simply and clearly; more detailed suggestions for applicants without representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to suggest amendments (Advices on Amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying grounds for rejection, amendments are suggested in the notice section 'Advices on Amendment'; the examiner should indicate related grounds for rejection when making suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions must be tied to the rejection grounds so applicant understands rationale and relationship to patentability objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to suggest amendments for novelty and inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may suggest amendments in cases: ① where dependent claims are allowable, suggest adding a technical element from allowable dependent claims to the claim needing amendment while explaining the reason; ② where no claim is allowable but the description discloses a technical element distinguishing from prior art, suggest adding that element; ③ where a dependent claim is allowable but description discloses a technical element that yields a more reasonable scope, examiner may suggest that element (and may suggest both options).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the reason/technical effect when suggesting elements. If selecting elements from multiple elements in a dependent claim or description, point to paragraphs/drawings evidencing the element and the technical effect. In some cases, indicate elements rather than full redrafting to avoid excessive claim drafting by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to suggest amendments for indefinite claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments may be suggested to overcome rejection for indefinite claims (e.g., delete vague term like 'high-speed' or replace with 'speed ranging from ㅇㅇ to ㅇㅇ' as described in the description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific numerical ranges or clear definitions from the description to remove indefiniteness; cite the paragraph in the description from which the specific wording is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid suggesting amendment to already patentable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: It is inappropriate to suggest amendment to claims that are already patentable (i.e., avoid proposing to add elements from patentable claims into other claims in a way that undermines granted patentable subject-matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: do not suggest adding a structure that is currently patentable as-is into another claim if that would be counterproductive; avoid undermining claim strategy by unnecessary incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessively narrowing the claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not suggest amendments that excessively narrow the scope of patent claims (e.g., combining multiple claims or adding many descriptive elements leading to undue narrowing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show suggestions that over-limit claims are inappropriate; examiner should balance overcoming rejection with retaining reasonable protection scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ambiguous suggestions of amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions must be specific; ambiguous advice (e.g., 'combine element X, Y, Z' without defining scope) is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous wording can mislead applicants and fail to resolve rejection; suggestions should indicate concrete elements or specific redrafting guidance when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid causing new grounds for rejection by suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should avoid suggesting amendments that could introduce ambiguity or relationships that create new grounds for rejection (e.g., adding an element that makes the relation between parts ambiguous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adding an element to a claim could cause ambiguity leading to new rejections, suggest adding it to an intermediate dependent claim rather than directly to the independent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on suggesting new matter or broadening at final-rejection stage
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not appropriate to suggest introduction of new matter or broadening a claim when notifying the grounds for final rejection necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing a final rejection necessitated by amendment, suggestions must not propose adding new subject-matter or enlarging claim scope beyond what was present in the relevant baseline (original filing or prior amendment as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio amendment — authority and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may amend a specification, drawings or an abstract ex‑officio to correct obvious errors (Article 66-2). If intending to amend ex‑officio, the examiner should notify the applicant together with service of a certified copy of decision to grant (Article 66-2(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant cannot accept parts/all of the ex‑officio amendment, they should file a written argument to the Commissioner before paying the patent fee. Where applicant files such an argument, parts or all of the ex‑officio amendment shall be deemed not made and the decision to grant shall be deemed revoked (with limited exception for abstract-only changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope extension of ex-officio amendment (since March 2017) with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of ex‑officio amendment has been extended to allow examiners to amend deficiencies which would otherwise be subject to grounds for rejection if those deficiencies are considered obvious mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite the extension, ex‑officio amendment should be applied complementally and not broadly — applicants remain principally responsible for making out the application and Article 47 strictly defines entitlement, time limits, and scope of amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of 'obvious mistakes' for ex-officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Obvious mistakes' mean that a person skilled in the art should easily recognize obvious mistakes in specification/drawings/abstract and it can be easily anticipated how documents are amended as the original intention can be clearly understood from the specification, written argument and common general technical knowledge as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters include standard Korean terms or simple typos, an omitted word, inconsistency of drawing numerals, redundant writing, errors in simple explanation of drawing (wrong figure number, mislabeled numerals), wrong indication of representative figure, inconsistency in title between description and application, etc. Ex-officio amendment not permitted if the applicant's original intention cannot be clearly understood.
